purpose: Holds a Modal's actions at the bottom of the card, primary last, with an optional step counter or link at the start. It is also the SheetFooter of a Sheet.

notFor.case: Actions at the bottom of a Popover panel.
Actions at the bottom of a dropdown menu.
A row of related buttons outside a dialog.

Default.meaning: At rest; it has no interactive state of its own.
Default.visual: Actions row; the leading text in Content/secondary (Type/caption). Surface plain draws a top hairline in Border/subtle (Stroke/divider); tray and simple drop it (Stroke/none) and simple also removes the padding (Spacing/0).

a11y.role: None of its own: a region inside the Modal's dialog (Radix Dialog).
a11y.keyboard: No keys of its own. Inside the open Modal, Tab / Shift+Tab cycle through its buttons in the focus trap; Escape closes the dialog and returns focus to the trigger.
notes: Put the primary action last in inline order; the buttons keep their own focus order.
Stacked gives full-width buttons for narrow viewports.

openQuestions: Top stroke: Figma draws none on ModalFooter (6 variants, e.g. node 966:26) while the contract binds Border/subtle. Which is right? (finding PAR-001 ModalFooter root.stroke)

Surface (plain · tray · simple) is a code axis with no Figma variant, and the Storybook control does not match it (finding PAR-001 ModalFooter story/Surface). Should Surface become a Figma axis, or stay code-only?
The layout prop is typed 'inline' | 'stacked' but the Figma Layout axis also has equal. When is equal used, and should the prop accept it?
